item.description:
Small Business Services | Procurement | Intent to Award | Due: 2026-10-09 | Flagged: Sole-source / non-competitive

The NYC Department of Small Business Services is entering into a Negotiated Acquisition Extension Contract with New York Committee for Occupational Safety and Health Inc to provide site safety training in the borough of Manhattan. Local Law 196 (2017) establishes Site Safety Training requirements for workers at most construction sites in the City of New York. Local Law 196 also requires that an agency designated by the Mayor will develop a program to provide equal access to the training required by Section 3321 of the New York City Building Code. The New York City Department of Small Business Services (SBS) has been designated to provide such a training program and to ensure that these essential safety standards are in place to protect the lives of construction workers and the public consistent with the requirements outlined in the local law. The contract term will be from 7/1/2026 to 6/30/2027, in the amount of $344,203.00

The services required under this contract are required to maintain the level of services required to be provided to construction site safety day laborer individuals until a new solicitation can be released and a new contract awarded.

NOTICE OF INTENT TO REQUEST RELEASE OF FUNDS (NOI RROF)

On or about October 8, 2026, the City of New York (the City) anticipates submitting a request to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) for the release of $51,780,000 of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds authorized under the Housing and Community Development Act of 1992, to undertake the Citys Demolition Program citywide, for a period of five years.

The Alternative Enforcement Program (AEP) is intended to address the serious physical deterioration of the most distressed buildings in New York City. Through AEP, the NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) can order the property owner to repair or replace building systems as well as to address violations. item.description:
Youth and Community Development | Procurement | Award | $514K | Vendor: Grand Street Settlement Inc | Flagged: Sole-source / non-competitive

The Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD), as the designated Community Action Agency for New York City, administers the federal Community Services Block Grant (CSBG) program to combat poverty and provide services that empower low-income individuals and families to achieve self-sufficiency. To maximize the impact of CSBG funding, DYCD targets funds to low-income neighborhoods designated as Neighborhood Development Areas (NDAs). The NDA Initiative promotes community-level engagement to ensure that services address the most pressing needs within each community. Programs use a strength-based approach, partnering with participants to build upon existing assets and capacities to achieve personal and community goals. Given the specialized nature of these services and the need for continuity and responsiveness to local community conditions, DYCD seeks approval to use the Negotiated Acquisition method in accordance with PPB Rule §3-04(b)(2)(i)(D). This approach allows the agency to negotiate directly with qualified community-based organizations (CBOs) that have demonstrated experience, trust, and engagement within their respective NDAs.

CORRECTED NOTICE

This is a notice that The Department of Youth & Community Development (DYCD) is seeking comments from the public about the proposed contract below.

 

Contract Type: Contract

Contractor Name: Police Athletic League Inc

Contractor Address: 34 1/2 East 12th Street, New York, NY 10003

Scope of Service:  The Comprehensive After School System of New York City (COMPASS) offers a network of high-quality, no-cost programs located in New York City Public Schools (NYCPS) and charter schools housed in NYCPS buildings. Serving both elementary and middle school students, COMPASS supports working families by providing enriching after-school care, school holiday programming, and summer services (for elementary programs). Designed to help students in Kindergarten through 8th grade thrive both academically and socially, COMPASS ensures that learning and development continue well beyond the school day.

Contract Amount: $5,904,468.00

Term: August 1, 2026 through August 31, 2032

item.title: COMPASS Programs in Public Schools - Middle
item.description:

COMPASS and SONYC is one of DYCD's largest programs, with over 820 programs collectively throughout the five boroughs. Families rely on these programs to provide elementary and middle school students, during after school hours, summer and on holidays, programing which includes educational support, recreation, enrichment, and cultural activities to support and strengthen the overall development of our youth. item.title: FY27- RSQ- New Contract/Family Support Services
item.description:
Health and Mental Hygiene | Procurement | Award | $11.8M | Vendor: New York Foundling | Flagged: Contract value ≥ $1M

The New York State Office of Mental Health ('OMH') requires the NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene to contract with The New York Foundling Hospital d/b/a The New York Foundling (Contractor) will provide ongoing training, capacity building, and technical support to service providers working in family-serving community-based organizations and agencies to enhance their ability to use strength-based, culturally relevant positive parenting and family support models in their work. These services will be implemented as the Strong Families and Communities Center (The SFC Center) at New York Foundling (The Center). These efforts will strengthen family relationships and empower parents/caregivers to improve the social-emotional health and development of children and youth. The training and technical support will focus on parenting and peer support models that providers will then use in their work with families.
